text: You're in your car, ready to go. Your map app suggests a route. Shorter should be faster, right? You just want to get to your destination efficiently.
But the app recommends a path that looks much longer, winding through unfamiliar streets. It feels counter-intuitive, yet you decide to trust its guidance.
As you drive, the main road, which you *thought* was shorter, is jammed with coral red traffic. Your chosen path remains clear. Is this really faster?
Then it clicks. The app isn't just showing static distance; it's calculating real-time flow. Signal blue lines mean clear roads, while the main road is a slow, red crawl.
You arrive surprisingly quickly. Your old intuition, focused only on distance, ignored the dynamic, invisible system of traffic density. That was the cost.
Now, the next time your map suggests a winding path, you understand. You see the invisible currents of traffic, no longer fooled by static lines.
